name: gods-eye-view
description: A spy satellite simulator in your browser, except the data is real. Live open source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe.
one_liner: A free website that shows a live, spinnable 3D globe with real flights, ships, satellites, earthquakes, and public cameras — like a spy-movie command center anyone can open in a browser.
buyer: A media company or corporate training studio that needs dramatic, real-time 'world situation' visuals for broadcasts, briefings, or simulations without building custom mapping software.
business_use_cases: A news channel licenses a hosted, branded version to show live flight/ship disruptions during breaking-news segments instead of static maps.
A logistics or insurance company embeds the live-tracking layer into a client dashboard to visualize shipping and flight risk in real time.
An events company builds immersive 'mission control' installations for conferences and trade-show booths using the globe as a centerpiece.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted, white-labeled version with a company's branding and data layers for a monthly fee.
Sell a one-time 'custom build' service adding a client's proprietary data feed (fleet, assets, stores) onto the globe.

steal_this: Fork it, add one company's fleet-tracking feed as a custom layer, and pitch it this weekend to a local logistics or delivery company as a live ops dashboard.
